blocker: Investigated for this closure (see reports/gba_playtest_issue13_closure.md "Combat residual" for the full trace): from the #11 debug-only "Fast Boot: Chapter 2" launcher's clean-boot roster (Eirika/Seth/Gilliam/Franz/Moulder in Blue, Ross in Green, Bone+bandits in Red -- confirmed live via gUnitArrayBlue/Red/Green EWRAM probes at fixed addresses derived from this build's own symbol table, never a raw offset guess), every Blue unit is 6-14 tiles from the nearest Red unit at first-player-phase, so no unit can reach attack range in a single turn -- single-turn combat is not just unattempted, it is geometrically unreachable from this launcher's own start-of-turn placement. Reaching a second player turn requires first complying with this chapter's own mandatory, tutorial-flagged Guide hint chain (rescue Ross, regroup near Vanessa, visit a village -- each is real scripted story content, not a harness defect), which was driven to completion with ordinary A/directional input only: doing so reaches a genuine "End" System-Menu item (absent until every unit has acted), confirming it ends Player Phase (gPlaySt.faction reads FACTION_ENEMY/0x80) and drives real, deterministic enemy-AI repositioning (three Red units' xPos/yPos probes changed turn-over-turn). That is a genuine, reproducible turn-resolution proof, but the Enemy Phase then stops advancing (unit positions and the framebuffer both stay byte-identical for several thousand further frames, tried both with and without extra input) before any attack resolves -- an unexplained stall specific to this exact debug-launcher-plus-input path that needs further, likely proc/event-level, investigation before it can be trusted as a scenario. A savestate, save file, or other generated binary remains prohibited as a shortcut past either blocker. Enabling this stub requires either resolving that stall (or finding a different deterministic route to a live attack) and a checkpoint that independently proves actor/target HP before and after a real combat round -- framebuffer/timing similarity alone is never sufficient.
description: Schema-ready placeholder for deterministic combat capture (actor/target HP, round result, death/exp).
